ted2544bc: 1. Logging in and finding your way around
t414c74e1:
How Turnera is used day to day in a centre: booking, charging, and knowing what happened. It is written for
  the person at the front desk, not for the person who writes the software.
tee517e71:
Turnera opens in the browser, with the centre's address and the username and password you were given.
    There is nothing to install and it works the same on the front desk computer, on a tablet or on a phone.
t693db287:
This is not red tape: the application records who did each thing, and
    with a shared account that information is worth nothing at all. What is more, each user sees only their own part — the
    receptionist has no need to open the clinical record, and the physiotherapist has no need to see the till.
teb502b7f: Each person has their own user account.

    you set up now and then (catalogue, stock, staff) and what you only look at (reports and settings).
tee169027:
If one of those entries is missing for you it is not a fault: your user account does not have that permission.
    Whoever administers the centre can give it to you.
